algorithm.Title: Earwax - Female (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Female
Definition: Qatar-localized UAT-only adult and pediatric pathway for suspected earwax, screening for sudden hearing loss, infection, perforation, foreign body and contraindications to irrigation or drops.

questions.Question: Is ear pain, discharge, fever, or acute illness the main concern rather than wax blockage?
questions.Information: Ear pain or acute ear illness belongs in the Earache pathway.

questions.Question: Have symptoms lasted more than 5 days despite home treatment, or is there a severe blockage preventing hearing?
questions.Information: NHS.UK earwax guidance recommends primary-care review for symptoms lasting more than 5 days or a severe hearing blockage.

questions.Question: Is this a recent, mild earwax blockage with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends softening oil drops as first-line home treatment.

advice.Title: Urgent earwax review
Content: Arrange review by a primary-care clinician or nurse - the wax may need professional removal by irrigation, microsuction, or gentle scraping.
Call Back If: pain or discharge develops.

advice.Title: Assessment before earwax treatment
Content: Do not insert objects, use ear candles or irrigate the ear. Arrange clinician/pharmacist review before drops are selected because age, eardrum status, surgery/tubes, infection, pregnancy and allergies must be checked.
Call Back If: sudden hearing loss; pain, discharge, bleeding, fever or dizziness.

searchwords: ear feels blocked up with wax

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Has anything already been tried, including drops, irrigation, candles or cotton buds?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 18 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What is the exact age; is the patient pregnant; and are there sudden hearing loss, pain, discharge, bleeding, dizziness, previous perforation/surgery, tubes, diabetes, immune suppression, foreign body or safeguarding concerns?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 18 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Child assessment adds safe-caregiver observations without inventing a different clinical threshold.
